title: World Sees Six Straight Days Above 2°C Warming Limit for the First Time
title_zh: 全球首次出现连续六天升温超工业化前水平2°C纪录
source_name: The Guardian — Six Consecutive Days 2°C Above Preindustrial Levels
summary_zh: 2026年11月下旬，欧盟哥白尼气候变化服务局的数据显示，全球地表温度有史以来首次连续六天维持在较工业化前水平（1850—1900年基线）高出至少2°C的水平，并在11月23日达到2.24°C的峰值。科学家指出，这是长期燃烧化石燃料导致全球变暖与强厄尔尼诺现象叠加的结果。尽管连续六天的短期高温尚不代表《巴黎协定》长期目标被永久突破，但专家警告这释放出全球变暖可能正在加速的强烈信号，凸显出加快减排和转向清洁能源的紧迫性。
paragraphs: In late November 2026, Earth reached a troubling climate milestone. According to data from the European Union's Copernicus Climate Change Service, global surface temperatures stayed at least 2°C above pre-industrial levels for six consecutive days for the first time in recorded history. Measured against the 1850–1900 baseline, the daily average peaked at 2.24°C on Monday, 23 November. Previously, temperatures had crossed the 2°C mark only during brief spikes in November 2023 and February 2024, making this six-day streak both longer and hotter than any earlier event.

Climate scientists quickly warned that the record cannot be treated as ordinary seasonal weather. Samantha Burgess of the Copernicus Climate Change Service described the readings as an exceptional global temperature anomaly that reflects how much the planet has already warmed. While individual days can rise and fall, pushing past 2°C for nearly a full week shows that baseline conditions are shifting upward. Researchers noted that the previous daily record of 2.05°C, set in late 2023, was decisively broken during this warm spell.

Several forces combined to drive the unusual spike in heat. Long-term warming from burning fossil fuels has steadily raised average global temperatures over recent decades, leaving the climate system hotter before natural cycles even begin. On top of that human-driven trend, a strong El Niño weather pattern is approaching its peak in the Pacific Ocean. During an El Niño event, warmer surface waters release extra heat into the atmosphere, temporarily pushing global temperatures even higher than normal.

Scientists emphasized that six hot days do not mean the world has permanently failed to meet international climate goals. Under the 2015 Paris Agreement, countries promised to hold long-term global warming well below 2°C and to pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C. Because those targets are measured over decades rather than single weeks, a short streak does not officially breach the agreement. Still, experts such as Zeke Hausfather of Berkeley Earth cautioned that repeated short-term records are an alarming signal that global heating may be accelerating.

The new figures add fresh urgency to global efforts to cut greenhouse gas emissions and prepare vulnerable communities for extreme heat. Even temporary surges above 2°C can intensify heatwaves, strain power grids, and place heavy pressure on crops and water supplies. Researchers stressed that every fraction of a degree matters for reducing future damage. Rapidly expanding clean energy and phasing down coal, oil, and gas remain essential steps to prevent today's rare extremes from becoming everyday weather.
paragraphs_zh: 2026年11月下旬，地球迎来了一项令人忧心的气候节点。根据欧盟哥白尼气候变化服务局的数据，全球地表温度有史以来首次连续六天维持在较工业化前水平高出至少2°C的水平。以1850年至1900年的平均温度为基线衡量，日均升温幅度的峰值在11月23日星期一达到2.24°C。此前，全球气温仅在2023年11月和2024年2月的短暂峰值期间突破过2°C关口，因此这一次长达六天的高温期比以往任何一次都持续得更久、温度也更高。
气候科学家很快警告称，这一纪录绝不能被当作普通的季节性天气来看待。哥白尼气候变化服务局的萨曼莎·伯吉斯将这些数据描述为一次非同寻常的全球温度异常，反映出地球已经变暖了多少。尽管单日气温会有起有落，但连续将近一周突破2°C表明，全球气候的基准状态正在向上推移。研究人员指出，此前在2023年底创下的2.05°C单日最高纪录，在此次暖期中被明显打破。
多种力量共同促成了这次反常的高温飙升。近几十年来，燃烧化石燃料带来的长期变暖稳步推高了全球平均气温，使气候系统在自然周期发挥作用之前就已经处于更热的状态。在这一由人类活动驱动的趋势之上，太平洋上一个强劲的厄尔尼诺天气模式正接近峰值。在厄尔尼诺现象期间，较温暖的表层海水会向大气释放额外热量，从而暂时把全球气温推得比平时更高。

科学家强调，连续六天的高温并不意味着世界已经永久性地未能实现国际气候目标。根据2015年《巴黎协定》，各国承诺将长期全球变暖幅度控制在远低于2°C的水平，并努力将其限制在1.5°C以内。由于这些目标是以数十年而非单个星期为尺度来衡量的，短暂的连续高温在官方定义上并不构成对协定的突破。即便如此，伯克利地球研究所的齐克·豪斯法瑟等专家仍警告称，反复出现的短期高温纪录是一个令人警觉的信号，表明全球变暖可能正在加速。
最新数据为全球削减温室气体排放以及帮助脆弱社区应对极端高温的行动增添了新的紧迫感。即便是暂时突破2°C，也可能加剧热浪、让电网承受重压，并对农作物和水资源供应造成巨大冲击。研究人员强调，每减少零点几度的升温，都对降低未来损失至关重要。迅速扩大清洁能源规模并逐步减少煤炭、石油和天然气的使用，仍然是防止如今罕见的极端天气变成日常天气的关键举措。

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A new European plan to replace the 2015 Paris Agreement with weekly temperature limits.
Earth experiencing six consecutive days at least 2°C above pre-industrial levels, its causes, and what the record means for climate goals.
Why scientists believe the Pacific El Niño pattern has completely stopped affecting global weather.
How power grids in Europe successfully prevented heatwaves during November 2026.
questions.explanation: 全文围绕全球首次连续六天出现地表温度较工业化前水平高出至少2°C的纪录展开，介绍了相关观测数据、化石燃料与厄尔尼诺现象的共同作用，以及科学家对这一短期高温与《巴黎协定》长期目标关系的解读。其他选项均与原文内容不符。

evidence.quote: According to data from the European Union's Copernicus Climate Change Service, global surface temperatures stayed at least 2°C above pre-industrial levels for six consecutive days for the first time in recorded history.

questions.prompt: According to the third paragraph, how does an El Niño event contribute to higher global temperatures?
options: It blocks sunlight from reaching the Pacific Ocean for several decades.
It reduces the amount of fossil fuels burned by industrial countries.
Warmer surface waters in the Pacific Ocean release extra heat into the atmosphere.
It reverses long-term human-driven warming before natural cycles begin.
questions.explanation: 第三段明确说明，在厄尔尼诺现象期间，太平洋较温暖的表层海水会向大气释放额外热量，从而暂时把全球气温推得比平时更高。其他选项均不符合原文表述。

evidence.quote: During an El Niño event, warmer surface waters release extra heat into the atmosphere, temporarily pushing global temperatures even higher than normal.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from the fourth paragraph about the 2015 Paris Agreement targets?
options: They evaluate global warming using multi-decade averages rather than brief weekly spikes.
They are automatically cancelled as soon as daily temperatures pass 2°C for six days.
Scientists believe the 1.5°C goal only applies to temperatures in the Pacific Ocean.
Experts see short-term temperature records as harmless events that require no attention.
questions.explanation: 第四段指出，《巴黎协定》的目标是以数十年而非单个星期为尺度来衡量的，因此连续六天的高温并不会正式意味着永久突破协定目标；但科学家仍将其视为令人警觉的信号。由此可推断，协定目标评估的是跨越几十年的长期平均变化，而非短暂的单周飙升。

evidence.quote: Because those targets are measured over decades rather than single weeks, a short streak does not officially breach the agreement.
